summary.name: MacSift
summary.one_liner: MacSift is a free, open-source macOS disk cleaner that groups junk files by the app they belong to and moves them to the Trash instead of deleting them permanently.
use_cases: Free up disk space on a Mac safely
Clear app caches and logs by application
Find large files in the home folder
Review old downloads and orphaned app data before deleting
Delete iOS device backups or Time Machine snapshots with review
summary.what_it_does:
MacSift scans a Mac across eleven categories, including caches, logs, temporary files, Xcode junk, developer caches, unused app data, mail attachments, Time Machine snapshots, large files, old downloads, and iOS backups. It groups results by the owning app (for example, collapsing a Safari cache folder into one row) and shows the largest files, a representative path, and actions like Reveal in Finder, Quick Look, and copy path. Selected items are moved to the Trash via FileManager.trashItem, and a dry run is on by default. Each cleaning run ends with an itemized report of deleted, failed, and freed space.</what_it_does>
<parameter name="pricing">open source
notable: Groups files by owning app using rule-based grouping per category
Moves items to the Trash rather than deleting permanently, with dry run on by default
Hard-blocks /System, /usr, /bin and /sbin in the cleaning engine; extra warning above 10 GB
No telemetry, ad-hoc signed, cleaning engine source is about 120 lines and readable
caveats: Pre-built release is Apple Silicon only; first launch needs right-click → Open because the app is ad-hoc signed without a Developer ID
